subject: PhenomAI VPC — sudden p95/p99 latency & 502s (req exec brief + mitigation)
messages:
From: Asha Roy <asha.roy@phenomai.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: support@phenomai.com
Date: 2026-08-28T22:14:00Z
Subject: Sudden latency spike and 502s in our VPC deployment (urgent)

Markus —

We're seeing a problematic spike across our private vpc cluster that started ~21:40 UTC: p95 and p99 token latency both doubled and we began seeing intermittent 502s for the text-generation route. Attached is a snapshot from our Grafana over the last 90m and the server list. Impacting customer-facing inference for 2 EU regions.

Key points:
- p95 jumped from ~180ms -> ~420ms; p99 up to ~1.2s
- 502 rate ~0.6% of requests in last 20m; downstream queue depth on node-3 shows surges
- This cluster is on the Redwood Private image we upgraded last week (model v2.3.0, compiled with the new attention kernel)

We need immediate remediation and an exec-level update for our CTO and VP Sales — SLAs are sensitive here. Can Redwood triage now and propose a short mitigation (traffic diversion/canary) and a rollback path?

Thanks,
Asha
Asha Roy
Head of Ops, PhenomAI
asha.roy@phenomai.com
+44 7700 123456
(Attachments: phenom_latency_snapshot_20260828.png, phenom_serverlist_20260828.txt)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Asha Roy <asha.roy@phenomai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-28T22:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike and 502s in our VPC deployment (urgent)

Asha —

Thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We're standing up a triage war room now. Laura (SRE lead for Private EU) and Marissa (Customer Success) are looped in. Initial ask: please push the redwood probe traces (INF-2247) to the Drive link if possible — that'll speed root cause.

Immediate mitigation plan (short):
1) We will route 25% of traffic away from the affected hotshard to a warm backup pool (1.5x capacity) for the next 30m.
2) If latency doesn't fall in 15m, we will rollback the model runtime to v2.2.7 (the prior image) and hold canary traffic on v2.3.0 at 0%.
3) Request Phenom enable short-term increased concurrency limits on client-side retry to avoid thundering.

Laura: can you confirm availability of warm pool and whether KV cache priming will be safe to enable for this cluster?

I will prepare an exec one-pager and the timeline for the CTO — expected war room @ 23:00 UTC unless you ask otherwise.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Site Reliability — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
(Attachment: redwood_probe_trace_INF-2247.zip)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, Asha Roy <asha.roy@phenomai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-28T22:33:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike and 502s in our VPC deployment (urgent)

Asha / Markus —

We're in the war room. Quick findings from the first 10m of traces:
- Multiple GPU-side decoder OOMs observed on node-3 and node-4 correlating with higher batch sizes coming from a sudden traffic pattern shift (customers running larger batched requests).
- The new attention kernel in v2.3.0 shows increased tail latency on long-sequence prompts in our test harness (we're seeing a pacing issue we haven't seen in pre-prod).
- KV cache warmup is currently disabled on that image due to an earlier compatibility flag; enabling it should reduce tokens computed per request but needs a short warm period (~5-10 min).

Confirming immediate actions we've kicked off:
- Diverting 30% traffic to warm pool now (live): route-change id rchg-9876
- Spun up a small fallback fleet on v2.2.7 and started canarying 10% of traffic there
- Beginning controlled enable of KV cache on 2 nodes (node-5, node-6) to prime caches

We will watch for p95 drop and 502 reduction. If OOMs persist we'll force full rollback.

I'll post a short exec-summary in 20m.

Laura Bennett
SRE Lead, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
(Attachment: initial_trace_excerpt.txt)

Date: 2026-08-28T23:05:00Z

Asha —

We're monitoring with you. Two asks from the CS side:
- Could you share any recent client-side rollout notes or traffic pattern changes (e.g., new batched inference from a partner)? That would help rule out a customer-driven spike.
- If you need an SLA credit request escalated, please send a one-line impact summary (customers, approx % of revenue affected) and we'll loop in Sales Ops.

We'll include the exec one-pager for your CTO in ~30m.

— Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Asha Roy <asha.roy@phenomai.com>

Date: 2026-08-29T00:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike and 502s in our VPC deployment (urgent)

Thanks team —

Quick replies:
- We pushed a partner batch test at 21:21 UTC that increased typical batch sizes; that partner was on a staged rollout and we failed to throttle (my fault). Sharing partner rollout notes now (drive link).
- Impact: 3 enterprise customers in EU experiencing >30% degraded throughput; estimated revenue exposure ~4% of monthly ARR. We will followup with a short SLA/cotact note for Sales Ops.

We're good with the temporary routing and canary. Please keep us posted on rollback triggers — our CTO wants a 30-minute cadence.

— Asha

(Attachment: partner_rollout_notes_v1.pdf)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Asha Roy <asha.roy@phenomai.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T14:38:00Z
Subject: Re: PhenomAI VPC — remediation summary and next steps (exec brief attached)

Asha —

Post-war-room summary for your CTO / VP Sales:
- Root cause (short): Interaction of a new attention kernel + unprimed KV cache + sudden partner-driven batch-size shift causing decoder memory pressure and request pacing that amplified tail latency.
- Short-term mitigation completed: 30% traffic diversion to warm pool, 10% canary on v2.2.7; KV cache primed on two nodes — p95 down ~38% and 502 rate fell to 0.12% after 45m.
- Next actions (24h): full staged rollback to v2.2.7 if no further regression; we will run a regression test for the v2.3.0 attention kernel on a copy of your workload with the partner pattern to identify kernel tuning.
- Exec ask: agree a runbook change so that any partner-side batch rollout has a mandatory throttle gating for first 72h.

Attached is a 1-page executive brief and the timeline of actions we executed. If you want a brief with the CTO and our VP Product, let's schedule a 30-min sync.

We will keep the war room open until midnight UTC tonight and provide a 3:00 UTC follow-up.

— Markus Klein
Director, Site Reliability — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
(Attachments: mk-exec-brief-phenomai-20260829.pdf)
